analysis:
Only head text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1-860) was supplied. No patch hunks or base text, so the exact changed lines are unknown. I checked the whole excerpt against the threat model. It is documentation only and changes no code or controls.

Security-relevant statements, all consistent with the canonical context:
- Logout (lines 431-480, A-008, T-053): it stops the provider, takes the single-instance and lifecycle locks, then sends the saved token as a Bearer credential to its recorded issuer's /v1/device/revoke. It uses a 10 s timeout, follows no redirects, and treats only HTTP 204 as confirmed revocation. Legacy tokens without issuer metadata are removed locally, remote revocation is stated as unconfirmed, and no URL is guessed. The host and port of the original coordinator are kept.
- Cache storage (lines 18-40, T-041): settings use a pinned volume UUID. Invalid or changed storage disables SSD caching and inference continues cold. The text claims no disk-firmware certification, which matches the T-041 limits. The daily write limit is saved and overrides the environment variable.
- Enroll and App Attest guidance (lines 548-562, T-052, T-057): guidance and the OS choice are not a serving grant. Legacy enrollment is limited to frozen identities.
- Switch and Autopilot (lines 227-320, 650-720): the text fails closed on missing coordinator receipts, and Autopilot shadow mode is not an activation.

The only defects I saw are cosmetic: jumbled flag tables around lines 582-600 and an empty 'Examples:' heading. They have no security impact. A later pass should check the actual diff for any weakened claim, such as a logout or revocation guarantee, if the diff becomes available.
